proof_summary: For \(n>0\), if \(2n\) had no decomposition into two primes, every entry in the matrix’s zeroth row would vanish, since a nonzero entry in column \(j\) would give primes \(n-j\) and \(n+j\) summing to \(2n\); thus the determinant would be zero. Taking \(n=2k+1\), the nonvanishing hypothesis gives the result for \(k\ge 60\), while explicit prime decompositions handle \(1\le k<60\).
